# filibuster

A Hugo theme that is a **permutation engine, not a fixed design**. One static,
read-only theme directory renders every customer site in the Inkwell pipeline;
everything that differs between two sites — content, imagery, and the entire
visual design — arrives as JSON at build time. The build is a pure function:

```
f(filibuster, data/*.json) -> static HTML
```

Rails never touches templates; the theme never touches the database. The JSON
contract (`contract_version: 1`) is the only coupling.

## How a build works

The exporter assembles a workspace and runs Hugo against it:

```
<workspace>/
├── hugo.toml                    # generated by Rails: baseURL, preview flag
├── data/
│   ├── site.json                # identity + the design block (see below)
│   ├── pages.json               # standing pages: slug, title, body_html
│   ├── author.json              # pen-name persona: name, bio_html, avatar
│   ├── books.json               # books: cover, description_html, distributors
│   ├── series.json              # series + ordered book slugs
│   └── posts.json               # blog posts, bodies pre-rendered as HTML
├── assets/images/               # covers + author photo
└── themes/filibuster -> …       # read-only symlink to a pinned theme version
```

The theme's **content adapters** (`content/**/_content.gotmpl`) materialize
pages directly from the JSON — one page per book, series, and post, plus
`/about/` and its sibling standing pages from `pages.json`. Rails emits no markdown and
no per-page stubs: adding a book to `books.json` adds a page to the site.
Each adapter asserts `contract_version` and fails the build loudly on drift.

Bodies (`*_html` fields) arrive pre-rendered and sanitized from Rails, so the
admin preview and the published page can never disagree, and no markdown
pipeline runs here.

## How the JSON customizes the design

Every visual decision is factored into an **independent design axis** with a
small closed vocabulary. The tenant's choices travel in `site.json`:

```json
"design": {
  "nav": "split",
  "palette": "nebula",
  "mode": "auto",
  "books": "yes",
  "cards": "spread",
  "catalog": "series",
  "alternate": "yes",
  "corners": "soft",
  "buttons": "soft",
  "hero_home": "yes",
  "hero": "right",
  "hero_book": "straight",
  "hero_many": "fan",
  "hero_bg": "page",
  "hero_scrim": "50",
  "font": "epic",
  "bio_home": "yes",
  "avatar": "frame",
  "avatar_side": "left",
  "bio_band": "stripe",
  "blog": "grid",
  "newsletter": "photo"
}
```

At build time `baseof.html` writes each value as a `data-*` attribute on
`<html>`:

```html
<html data-palette="nebula" data-cards="spread" data-hero="split" …>
```

All axis-conditional rules in `assets/css/*.css` (the numbered,
parallel-loaded modules) key off those
attributes — `html[data-palette="grimoire"]` swaps the CSS custom properties,
`html[data-hero="name"] .fk-hero-art { display: none }` restructures the
hero. No JavaScript touches layout, and no per-combination stylesheets exist,
which is what makes the axes truly independent: any combination composes.

| Axis | Options |
|---|---|
| `nav` | split, centered, grand, bare |
| `palette` | 15 dual-mode palettes (nebula, manuscript, mission, pulp, grimoire, pine, blush, boudoir, tide, rust, meadow, neon, bone, lumen, sandstone) — every token a designed `light-dark()` pair |
| `mode` | light, dark, auto (auto follows the reader's OS via `color-scheme`; zero JS) |
| `books` | yes, no — show or hide the books section on the home page (books/series pages still build and stay in the nav) |
| `cards` | spread, shelf, grid, panel, carousel, offset, fan |
| `catalog` | series (one card per series), books (every book) |
| `alternate` | yes, no — row layouts (spread/shelf/fan/offset) flip even rows |
| `corners` | square, crisp, soft, round — cover rounding on the Open Props radius scale (0 / 2px / 5px / 1rem), governs all book imagery |
| `buttons` | square, crisp, soft, round — button rounding on the same scale, overriding the palette's chrome radius |
| `hero_home` | yes, no — show or hide the hero on the home page |
| `hero` | structure only: none (copy only, centered), centered (one book below), right (one book beside, default), many (fanned covers) |
| `hero_book` | straight, 3d — how the featured cover renders (3d = CSS standing paperback; the designer shows it as a "Show as a 3D book" switch on one-book layouts) |
| `hero_many` | fan, staggered — the many-books arrangement (fanned hand of three, or a cascading row of four with the featured book in front) |
| `hero_bg` | page, gradient (two levels of the accent's hue), scrim, cover (blurred own art), banner (author-uploaded image) — copy color auto-derives from each backdrop's `--hero-ground` |
| `hero_scrim` | 0–100 by tens — black-veil opacity over the image backdrops (cover/banner); the auto-contrast copy follows the dial |
| `font` | 21 genre pairings (epic, classical, inscribed, thriller, noir, procedural, romance, commercial, ya-soft, ya-modern, ya-grotesque, gothic, clinical, starfall, dread, frontier, hearth, storybook, testament, ledger, verse) |
| `bio_home` | yes, no — show or hide the biography section on the home page |
| `avatar` | none (pure text), frame, round, square, organic |
| `avatar_side` | left, right |
| `bio_band` | none (plain page), stripe (color band), angled (slanted edges) — the band behind the bio section |
| `blog` | grid, list — the home page's "From the Blog" cards as a card grid or a vertical list |
| `newsletter` | photo, quiet, envelope, plane, megaphone, mailbox — the email-collection band: photo backdrop, plain, or an accent line-illustration beside the copy; headline/blurb/button ride `site.json`'s `newsletter` block |

Twenty-two axes, **~8.8 trillion combinations** from one theme. Fonts stay cheap
despite 21 pairings: one Google Fonts stylesheet (the manifest's
`fonts_url`) declares all the families, but browsers download only the
faces actually rendered. Custom overrides (any Google Font pairing; any
hex palette normalized to accessible shades via an OKLCH lightness policy)
arrive through `site.json`'s `fonts` and `colors` blocks; header content
(links, CTA button, logo with title-as-alt, hero banner, signup backdrop)
through its `nav`, `logo`, `banner`, and `newsletter_photo` fields; the
home-page section order through `home.sections`.

Readers ship **zero JavaScript**, with one policy exception: per-feature,
dependency-free, conditional islands — currently only `carousel.js`
(drag-to-scroll), included solely when `design.cards == "carousel"`.

Templates use superset markup: the hero partial, for example, renders the
pieces for every variant (covers, backdrop, fan list, marquee name) and CSS
shows or hides them per `data-hero` value. Hidden images are `loading="lazy"`,
so unused variants cost nothing until selected.

### One source of truth: `data/theme.json`

The axis vocabulary — keys, `data-*` attribute names, allowed values, labels,
defaults — and the named presets live in **`data/theme.json`**, the theme
manifest. It is consumed three ways:

1. **Hugo templates** read it (`hugo.Data.theme`) to emit and validate the
   `<html>` attributes. An unknown axis value fails the build — CSS attribute
   selectors fail silently, so the theme refuses to ship a subtly-wrong site.
   (Invoke Hugo without `--quiet`: that flag suppresses the `ERROR` text,
   leaving a failed build with an empty stderr. The exit code fails either
   way.)
2. **The SiteDesigner** (the Rails admin's design editor) renders its option
   rail from it — panes, cards, and labels are generated, never hand-listed.
3. **The Rails exporter** reads `themes/filibuster/data/theme.json` to
   validate a tenant's `design` block at export time, before Hugo runs.

Presets (Nebula, Bookshelf, Mission, Noir, Grimoire) each pin one value per
axis. They are **derived, not stored**: Rails persists only the seven axis
values; the preset label is computed by comparison, so there is no second
source of truth to drift.

## One design source, no client-side mutation

**The `design` block is the single source of truth.** Every build — preview
or reader — bakes the tenant's axes into `<html>` at build time; nothing on
the client ever changes the design. Authors design their site in the
**SiteDesigner** (Rails admin), which edits the design and triggers a
rebuild; the preview the author sees is a real Hugo build of this theme,
served in an iframe. (An earlier in-page "design switcher" existed for
exploration only and has been removed.)

`params.preview` in the generated `hugo.toml` is reserved for
designer-facing affordances (module anchors, edit affordances in the
SiteDesigner's preview iframe). Reader builds never include them.

## What renders where

| Path | Source | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | site + author + series + books + posts | `home.html` — slot engine: sections render in `site.json` `home.sections` order (default: hero, books, posts, bio, newsletter) |
| `/books/` | `books.json` + `series.json` | `books/section.html` — the library: cover grids grouped by series (series order), then a Standalone group for books without a series |
| `/books/<slug>/` | `books.json` | `books/page.html` — cover, buy links (via the `/buy/<track_id>` island when present), series pager |
| `/series/` | `series.json` + `books.json` | `series/section.html` — one series card per series (same cards as the home books section, so the `cards` axis applies) |
| `/series/<slug>/` | `series.json` + `books.json` | `series/page.html` — description, installment list |
| `/posts/` + `/posts/<slug>/` | `posts.json` | `section.html` / `posts/page.html` |
| `/about/`, `/privacy/`, `/terms/` | `pages.json` | `page.html` — one page per entry, at the slug it names |
| `/newsletter/` | `pages.json` (the `newsletter` slug) | `newsletter.html` — the invitation above the signup band `baseof` appends |

SEO (meta, Open Graph, Twitter cards) and JSON-LD (Person, BookSeries, Book,
BreadcrumbList) are generated from the same JSON on every page.

## Contract gaps, handled with defaults

The v1 contract has no newsletter service URL, no nav config, and no section
copy. The theme fills those with sensible derivations (mailto CTA from
`contact_email`, fixed nav, "The Books" / "From the Blog" headings, featured
book = newest `publication_date`). When the contract grows those fields, the
partials are the single place to wire them.
